title: Insurance Coverage & Patient Responsibility — Limits on Concurrent Coverage Records
content:
**Standard.** Under Insurance Coverage & Patient Responsibility a patient may hold at most 2 coverage records in pending verification or active status at the same time: 1 with the primary priority and 1 with the secondary priority. Terminated and not-eligible records stay on the account as history and do not count toward that limit.

## Clauses

1. **Concurrent limit.** At most 2 coverage records may be pending verification or active together — no more than 1 primary and no more than 1 secondary.
2. **Priorities the class admits.** A payer class may only take a priority its register entry admits. Medicare Supplement Plan G is therefore only ever secondary, and only behind Original Medicare Part B; and Medicare Advantage is never combined with a Medicare Supplement record.
3. **No duplicate enrollment.** No coverage record is added while a record with the same payer class and member id is pending verification or active.
4. **Third record.** A third concurrent record is refused until the record it replaces has been terminated from the payer's response.

## How the duplicate test is read

The duplicate test rests on the system's coverage records, read before a record is added, and it is tied to the patient and the member id being added: the same patient, the same member id and the same payer class, with the existing record in pending verification or active status. A record of that class and member id that is terminated or not eligible does not block the addition.

| Existing record for the same patient, payer class and member id | Status of that record | Addition of the new record |
|---|---|---|
| present | pending verification | not added |
| present | active | not added |
| present | terminated | not blocked by this test |
| present | not eligible | not blocked by this test |

## Worked cases (hypothetical)

- A patient holds an active Original Medicare Part B record as primary and an active Medicare Supplement Plan G record as secondary. A third record — say a Commercial PPO card — is refused until the record it replaces has been terminated from the payer's response.
- A patient holds an active Medicare Advantage PPO record. A Medicare Supplement Plan G record is not combined with it.
- A patient's earlier Commercial HMO record is terminated. It stays on the account as history and does not count toward the 2 concurrent records.
